You will be evaluated on how well you demonstrate the 21st Century Skills and meet the performance indicators of this event. Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the marketing lead at FERNWORKS COLLECTIVE, a plant shop and terrarium studio owned by the nine people who work in it. Every member holds one vote each, and the bylaws require a two-thirds vote of the members to change the legal structure the business operates under. An elected member-manager (judge) runs the shop day to day and brings the larger decisions to the floor.

Two years of sales records and website traffic point in the same direction. Most terrarium workshop seats are now booked online by people who live outside the neighborhood, and the workshop kits the studio ships out earn more per hour of staff time than anything sold across the counter. A rival, GLASSHOUSE GARDEN CO., is opening an online workshop line of its own this fall.

An outside investor has offered the money for a second studio and a shipping room, on the condition that FERNWORKS COLLECTIVE convert to a limited liability company. The members who work the floor have read the same records and disagree with what they show. They say the walk-in regulars and the hands-on workshops are what actually sells, and that one vote each is the reason experienced staff have stayed.

Converting to a limited liability company and taking the outside investment funds the growth the records point to, but it ends the one vote each rule that has kept the staff and hands a share of every decision to an outside owner. Staying a co-operative and paying for the second studio out of retained earnings keeps the vote, but takes four or five years and leaves the online workshop line to GLASSHOUSE GARDEN CO.

The member-manager (judge) has asked you to recommend which course to put to the members for a vote, and to explain what your recommendation does to the plan for reaching customers. The member-manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the elected member-manager (judge) of FERNWORKS COLLECTIVE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to bring one course to the members for a vote, and you would rather bring the right one. You want the marketing lead's recommendation on whether to convert to a limited liability company and take the outside investment or to stay a co-operative, and you want to hear what it means for how the studio reaches customers.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who carries the cost of the course you are recommending?
What would you say to the members who carry it?
